topic: After-hours queue checklist for property managers
hook: If the morning starts with cleanup, your after-hours workflow is still manual.

Start with the repeatable conversations that arrive when the office is closed but still need a clean next step before the team opens the next day. The right property management automation creates a usable queue, not a bigger mess.

slides.title: If the morning starts with cleanup,
slides.titleAccent: your after-hours workflow is still manual.
slides.body: Property teams should not open to stale leasing replies, half-filled maintenance requests, owner pings, vendor guesswork, and unassigned CRM follow-up.
slides.footer: Swipe for the 6 things the queue should already contain

slides.title: Every missed leasing call should leave a next step behind.
slides.body: After-hours calls should trigger SMS that captures intent, property interest, move timing, and reply routing before the lead disappears into voicemail.
slides.footer: Goal: a qualified lead, not a blind callback list

slides.title: No-show and no-reply renters should already be in motion.
slides.body: Tour reminders, rebooking prompts, and follow-up timing should be queued before staff open the CRM instead of rebuilt from memory and inbox threads.
slides.footer: Goal: the leasing team opens to live next steps

slides.title: Overnight requests should arrive dispatch-ready.
slides.body: Issue, urgency, unit, access notes, and photo requests should be captured up front so the morning team is triaging action, not collecting basics.
slides.footer: Goal: better triage before the first callback

slides.title: Standard repairs should already have a routing packet.
slides.body: Trade, property, resident context, approval state, and the next owner should be packaged so vendor handoffs do not start from a blank screen.
slides.footer: Goal: routing context attached before dispatch begins

slides.title: Important owner updates should be drafted from workflow data.
slides.body: Material leasing, maintenance, approval, or delay events can be summarized for review so owners hear the status without staff rewriting the timeline.
slides.footer: Goal: review-ready updates, not another status chase

slides.title: The queue should open with one record, one owner, one next action.
slides.body: AI voice, SMS, and CRM workflows should write back the summary, assignee, and follow-up state before the office opens so nobody retypes the same story.
slides.footer: Goal: the system opens with context already attached
